name: From Shells to the Euro
description: How people moved from cowries and silver bars to coins, paper, plastic and phone money, and what happened when currencies failed.

checkpoints.name: Shells and the first coins
checkpoints.note: People used shells, then stamped metal. Lydia struck some of the first coins, China made round cash with square holes, and Rome's silver denarius paid armies across the Mediterranean.

checkpoints.name: Gold of empires and caliphs
checkpoints.note: Rulers needed coins people trusted. Constantine's gold solidus lasted for centuries, caliphs put writing on the dinar, and China began issuing paper money, which merchants elsewhere only later copied.

checkpoints.name: Silver, ships and paper
checkpoints.note: Florence and Venice made gold coins that traded across borders, Spanish silver dollars moved around the world, and the Bank of England issued notes. In France the Mississippi Company bubble and later the assignats showed how fast paper money could be ruined.

checkpoints.name: Gold, wars and inflation
checkpoints.note: Nations tied their money to gold, then broke the link in crises and wars. Germany's hyperinflation and Russia's revolution showed how states can lose control of their currency.

checkpoints.name: The dollar age and after
checkpoints.note: After 1944 the dollar led world money until the link to gold ended in 1971. Cards, mobile money and Bitcoin followed, and Europe merged many currencies into the euro.
